title: Correction-exhaustion notification interpolates the stale snapshot referee name instead of the effective (corrected) name
evidence: webhooks.gleam:485-490: notification_dispatch.notify_reference_correction_exhausted(db, landlord_id, reference_call_id, row.contact_name, row.applicant_full_name) — row from find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql:19 which selects rc.contact_name (the immutable snapshot). form_handler.gleam:1309 passes row.contact_name from get_form_context_by_form_token.sql:13 (also rc.contact_name). The PR's own sweep change (sweep_due_reference_calls.sql:31) adopts the effective name: COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_name, ''), rc.contact_name) AS contact_name 'so the invite/reminder copy addresses the referee by name (§8.3)'.
detail: Exhaustion fires only when correction_cycles >= 1 — i.e. only after a successful correction, and correct_reference_call always sets corrected_name (validate_trio rejects an empty name). So every exhaustion notification names the PRE-correction referee: after the landlord corrects John Smith -> Jane Doe and the fresh invite to Jane Doe fails, the §7.9 notification reads 'Couldn't reach John Smith (...)' while the panel row and invites show Jane Doe. The awaiting-correction notification (webhooks.gleam:320) has the same snapshot source but is accurate (it fires before any correction exists). The two find queries that feed the exhaustion path were extended in this PR (correction_cycles/attempts/retention_due_at added) but the name column was left as the snapshot while the sweep query was switched to the effective name — an in-PR inconsistency in a new user-facing string.
recommended_fix: Select the effective name in find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql and get_form_context_by_form_token.sql (COALESCE(NULLIF(rc.corrected_name,''), rc.contact_name)) exactly as sweep_due_reference_calls.sql does, or pass the corrected name at the two exhaustion call sites.

title: update_trio's affected-row count is ignored: a same-owner cross-vacancy vacancy_id yields a 200 + audit with the application trio silently un-updated
evidence: actions_handler.gleam:211-214: case update_trio(tx, app_uuid, vacancy_uuid, row.ref_slot, trio) { Error(err) -> Error(DbFailure(err)) Ok(_) -> ...audit... } — the Ok arm ignores the row count. The trio UPDATEs are guarded WHERE id = $1 AND vacancy_id = $2 (update_application_referee_trio_landlord.sql:12-15), while correct_reference_call/substitute_reference_call are guarded on application_id only. run_action_with_prechecks (:574-591) verifies the vacancy belongs to the landlord but not that vacancy_uuid is the application's own vacancy.
detail: Reachable only via a malformed request (the client always posts the application's real vacancy id from the route), so no legit-path impact. But the write is partial: the reference_call corrected_* columns, the audit row and the 200 response all succeed while the application trio (read by the trigger's slot selection and the panel's Off-state chips) stays stale — a later re-start of the slot would invite the pre-correction contact. The handler's own doc comment claims the trio is updated ('the Off-state chips + future trigger reads then see the current referee'). Treating a 0-row trio update as an error inside the transaction would close the silent divergence.
recommended_fix: Map the trio update's row count: a 0-row result (vacancy mismatch) should roll back the transaction (e.g. reuse the NotSubstitutable/NotAwaitingCorrection error path or add a TrioNotUpdated variant) instead of proceeding to the audit + success payload.
